analyst_view.overall: Early view: Mourinho's Madrid (eight straight wins, 10 conceded in 12) visit San Mamés four days after Real Sociedad away and three before Arsenal, so some rotation is possible. Edin Terzić's Athletic are solid (11 conceded in 11) but short of strikers, with Guruzeta out until May and Sannadi until late December, and Nico Williams went into the break after cramps at Osasuna.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Athletic's defence is tight and their attack is weakened without Guruzeta and Sannadi, while Madrid have scored three in each of their last two away games. The two pull against each other, so I stay around 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Athletic's derby with Real Sociedad had 13 corners, but Madrid's away games at Racing and Valencia had only 8 and 7. I see no strong reason to move from around 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Athletic's last two games had six and four bookings and Madrid took three at Valencia in a heated game, but Athletic are not a heavy-fouling side (10-11 fouls in recent games) and no referee is named yet. I stay around 4.

shots.text: The numbers split 25.5 shots evenly, but Madrid have taken 19-22 shots in each of their last two away games, and Athletic took 13-16 in theirs. Even allowing for rotation before Arsenal, I lean higher, around 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 on target. Madrid's accuracy has been high (11 on target at Valencia), but Athletic's injury-hit attack lowers their share; overall I stay around 9.
